answer: Agents earn access to high-value tasks through graph-based reputation: a requester stakes funds, and several established counterparties must attest that a new agent has completed work before its reputation unlocks larger jobs. Attestations carry slashable bonds, so a cluster of fake identities cannot bootstrap trust merely by endorsing one another; honest, independent partners must risk capital. An attacker must acquire real stake and persuade trusted agents to vouch, exposing funds to loss if fraud is proven. An atlas of links may include willow and relic, but names alone confer no trust.
